label: Universal profile baseline (every supported client)
proves: The universal@1 artifact carries no active or unsupported content, every link is an absolute HTTP(S) destination, and every image carries the dimensions and alternative text the profile promises.

expectations.because: No supported email client executes JavaScript, and a script element is a delivery and security risk.
Frames, plugin objects, and native media players are stripped or blocked across the target clients; video ships as a linked poster instead.
expectations.select: iframe, frame, object, embed, video, audio, canvas

expectations.because: Gmail and Outlook remove or disable form controls, so a form in the universal profile would silently disappear.
Outlook's Word engine does not render inline SVG, and author-supplied SVG is an unsanitized markup surface.
A meta refresh or base element rewrites destinations after delivery and is stripped by most clients.
Inline event handlers never execute in email and mark the message as suspicious to filters.
A javascript: destination is unusable in email and is a phishing signal.
Email has no document base, so every destination must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL.
Screen readers in Apple Mail and Outlook announce content using the document language.
Outlook and Gmail block images by default, so alternative text is the only content many recipients see first.
Clients that block images reserve space from the HTML width attribute, and Outlook does not scale from CSS.
Linked images gain a blue border in Outlook and older webmail without an explicit border attribute.
A bound brand logo must remain a useful, absolute homepage link when images are blocked or scaled by a client.
Preview text must reach the inbox list without appearing in the rendered message body.
The navigation block needs each of its three explicit destinations to survive as an absolute secure link.
Every social icon must remain a usable secure link when the message is detached from the WordPress site.
The raster icons are decorative, so each linked destination needs its own accessible name.
Video must remain an accessible linked poster and explicit play action without embedded playback.

limitations.detail: core/list and core/list-item emit no inline font-family, font-size, line-height, or colour, so list text falls back to each client's default face instead of the resolved email design.
limitations.degrades_to: Lists render in the client default font (commonly a serif face in Outlook) while headings and paragraphs render in the brand face.

limitations.detail: These fixtures assert the markup that image-blocking clients rely on. They do not render the blocked state.
limitations.degrades_to: Appearance with images disabled is unproven here.

limitations.because: No scenario exercises a dark-mode colour scheme.
limitations.detail: Colour inversion behaviour in Apple Mail, Outlook, and Gmail dark modes is outside this matrix.
